window: Retrospective — the administration's first twelve days

stories.headline: Executive order directs agencies to designate cartels as foreign terrorist organizations
stories.body: Executive Order 14157, signed January 20, 2025 and published in the Federal Register on January 29, directs the Secretary of State to recommend cartels and transnational gangs for designation as Foreign Terrorist Organizations and Specially Designated Global Terrorists. It sets a policy of the total elimination of these organizations' presence in the United States and directs the Attorney General and DHS to prepare for possible use of the Alien Enemies Act.

stories.headline: Pentagon orders 1,500 additional troops to the southern border
stories.body: The Defense Department announced the deployment of 1,500 additional active-duty personnel — 1,000 soldiers and 500 Marines — plus two C-17s, two C-130s and UH-72 Lakota helicopters to the US-Mexico border on January 22, raising the active-duty total to roughly 4,000. Officials said the troops would provide real-time situational awareness of persons, vehicles, vessels and aircraft and support CBP operations.

stories.headline: Houston money-laundering takedown puts 29 in custody in CJNG-linked case
stories.body: The U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Texas announced on January 24 that 22 people were arrested in the Houston area, with 29 total in custody, on money laundering and narcotics indictments following a 21-month OCDETF investigation into a trade-based laundering network allegedly serving the Jalisco New Generation Cartel. Investigators seized multi-hundred-kilogram quantities of cocaine, heroin, methamphetamine and marijuana over the course of the probe, along with 17 firearms and about $1 million.

stories.headline: Alleged Sinaloa Cartel cell leader extradited from Mexico to San Diego
stories.body: Octavio Leal-Hernandez, 44, known as Chapito Leal, was extradited from Mexico and arraigned in federal court in San Diego on January 23. Prosecutors allege he led a Sinaloa Cartel cell aligned with the Beltran-Leyva faction that moved large shipments of methamphetamine, cocaine, heroin and marijuana from Tijuana into California. He pleaded not guilty and was held without bond.

stories.headline: US-Mexico cooperation dismantles Nogales fentanyl pipeline
stories.body: The U.S. Attorney's Office for the District of Arizona announced on January 24 that Mexican authorities had arrested organization leader Heriberto Jacobo Perez and Jesus Bernardo Rodriguez in Nogales, Sonora, seizing a large quantity of fentanyl pills, other controlled substances, two firearms, four vehicles and two buildings. Seven people were separately indicted in the United States over the same pipeline through the Mariposa Port of Entry.

stories.headline: Senior FARC trafficker sentenced to 78 months for cocaine importation
stories.body: Aldemar Soto-Charry, 64, known as El Ingeniero, was sentenced on January 24 to 78 months in federal prison for conspiring to import cocaine into the United States. The highly ranked FARC member told DEA sources his organization moved more than 1,000 kilograms of cocaine on a regular basis and could supply up to 2,000 kilograms every few weeks. He was arrested in Colombia in 2019 and extradited in August 2024.

stories.headline: Two sentenced over multi-state rings tied to Aryan prison gangs
stories.body: Eric Smith, 54, of Tacoma and Sara Thompson, 39, of Bonney Lake were sentenced on January 31 to 12 years and 7 years respectively for conspiracy to distribute controlled substances as part of rings linked to the Aryan Family and Omerta prison gangs. The March 2023 takedown across Washington and Arizona involved 24 arrests and netted 830,000 fentanyl pills, 223 pounds of methamphetamine and 177 firearms.

stories.headline: Three sentenced in $4.7 million Kansas City meth and heroin conspiracy
stories.body: The U.S. Attorney's Office for the Western District of Missouri announced on January 31 sentences of 18 years, 16 years and 3 months, and 7 years for Jesus Morales-Garcia, Baltazar Flores-Norzagaray and Santiago Raul Mendieta-Sanchez. The conspiracy distributed more than 335 kilograms of methamphetamine and over 22 kilograms of heroin sourced from Mexico into the Kansas City region between 2020 and 2022.

stories.headline: Leader of social-media drug ring sentenced to 10 years in Washington
stories.body: Joel Adrian Valencia Rosas, 28, of Lakewood, Washington was sentenced on January 28 to 10 years for leading a South Puget Sound trafficking ring that used Snapchat and Instagram to recruit couriers. The investigation seized nearly 52 kilograms of cocaine, more than 23 kilograms of fentanyl pills and 131 kilograms of marijuana, including 200,000 fentanyl pills taken in a single 2023 traffic stop on Interstate 5.

stories.headline: New Jersey man convicted over China-sourced fentanyl analogues
stories.body: A federal jury convicted William Panzera, 51, of North Haledon, New Jersey on January 29 of conspiring to distribute 100 grams or more each of furanyl fentanyl and 4-fluoroisobutyryl fentanyl, and of international promotional money laundering. The 2014-2020 conspiracy distributed fentanyl analogues, MDMA, methylone and ketamine sourced from China, including counterfeit pills; eight co-conspirators had already pleaded guilty.

stories.headline: Brockton-area trafficking leader pleads guilty to fentanyl conspiracy
stories.body: Jonathan Melendez Decatro, 32, of Braintree, Massachusetts pleaded guilty on January 30 to conspiracy to distribute fentanyl. Prosecutors identified him as the leader of a large-scale Brockton-area fentanyl and cocaine organization sourcing directly from Colombia, Mexico and the Dominican Republic; investigators intercepted 2 kilograms of cocaine in 2021 and 1.5 kilograms of fentanyl mixed with xylazine in 2023.

stories.headline: Arizona task force seizes 1,659 pounds of meth and 208 pounds of fentanyl near Phoenix
stories.body: The Arizona Financial Crimes Task Force, working with the DEA, announced on January 29 that a January 27 traffic stop and follow-up residential search warrant in the Phoenix area yielded roughly 1,659 pounds of methamphetamine, 161 pounds of fentanyl pills (about 735,000 pills) and 47 pounds of fentanyl powder. Officials put the Arizona street value at about $3.4 million and said the investigation remained ongoing, with no arrest details released.

stories.headline: Colombia seizes 8.2 tonnes of cocaine at Buenaventura in shipment bound for Spain
stories.body: National Police anti-narcotics officers seized 8.2 tonnes of cocaine hidden in a container of mineral fertilizer at the Pacific port of Buenaventura on January 22, destined for Algeciras and onward to Toledo, Spain. President Gustavo Petro called it one of the largest cocaine seizures in Colombian history; the shipment moved through a shell company in the fertilizer and chemicals sector and was valued at roughly $453 million in Europe. No arrests were reported.

stories.headline: Ecuador finds 2.48 tonnes of cocaine in pineapple container bound for Germany
stories.body: Anti-narcotics officers inspecting a fruit container at the port terminal in Posorja, Guayaquil found 2,488 blocks weighing 2,475.5 kilograms of cocaine after a detection dog alerted on the shipment, which was destined for Germany. The inspection took place on January 25 and no one was detained.

stories.headline: Army destroys Clan del Golfo cocaine lab in Cesar, seizing 526 kilograms
stories.body: Soldiers of Infantry Battalion No. 14, working with the National Police anti-narcotics directorate, destroyed a cocaine laboratory in the Los Bagres area of San Martín, Cesar on January 26, seizing 526 kilograms of cocaine hydrochloride, 12 gallons of liquid precursors and 110 kilograms of solid precursors. Authorities said the lab, run by a Clan del Golfo structure, could produce up to two tonnes a month for markets including Mexico's Sinaloa Cartel. No arrests were reported.

stories.headline: ELN offensive reignites the war for Colombia's Catatumbo coca belt
stories.body: InSight Crime reported that the ELN's offensive against FARC dissidents in Catatumbo, Norte de Santander had killed at least 80 people and displaced some 11,000 residents. The region holds roughly 44,000 hectares of coca, concentrated in Tibú, and is a key cocaine corridor into Venezuela; President Petro suspended peace talks with the ELN over the attacks.

stories.headline: Petro declares state of internal commotion over Catatumbo violence
stories.body: The Colombian government published a decree on January 24 declaring a state of internal commotion covering eleven Norte de Santander municipalities, the Cúcuta metropolitan area and two Cesar municipalities, running to April 2025. The decree cites the ELN financing itself through drug trafficking and notes that Sardinata and Tibú alone held 27,329 hectares of coca in 2023, 63.3 percent of the region's total, against 381 homicides and more than 36,000 displaced people.

stories.headline: Colombian military reports 84 ELN fighters surrendered in Catatumbo offensive
stories.body: The Colombian Army reported the first results of its Catatumbo offensive around Tibú, Norte de Santander on January 25: 84 ELN members surrendered and 20 minors recruited by the group's Bloque Magdalena Medio were recovered. Troops also seized 55 long guns, 25 pistols, 80 mortar grenades, a tonne of explosives, 300 antipersonnel mines and more than 20,000 rounds of ammunition.

stories.headline: Infighting in Ecuador's Los Lobos turns El Oro into a battleground
stories.body: InSight Crime reported that infighting within Los Lobos, including the breakaway LobosSaoBox faction, had made El Oro one of Ecuador's most violent provinces, with 591 homicides in 2024 — 82 per 100,000. The fighting centres on control of cocaine routes through Machala's Puerto Bolívar, where more than 10 tonnes of cocaine had been seized by August 2024, alongside illegal gold mining revenues.

stories.headline: Gendarmería finds 200 packages of cocaine in abandoned pickup near Bolivian border
stories.body: Squadron 20 of Argentina's Gendarmería Nacional found an abandoned pickup truck early on January 28 on Provincial Route 5 near Colonia Santa Rosa in Orán, Salta province, close to the Bolivian border. It contained 200 packages of compacted white powder identified as cocaine. No arrests were reported and no total weight was released.

stories.headline: Venezuelan police kill Petare gang boss after six-year manhunt
stories.body: Wilexis Alexander Acevedo Monasterios, boss of the gang that had controlled the José Félix Ribas sector of Petare since 2017, was killed by CICPC officers during an operation in Filas de Mariche, Miranda state, announced January 22. Acevedo ran extortion, kidnapping, robbery and retail drug dealing and carried a $150,000 bounty.

stories.headline: Venezuela deploys military anti-drug operation on the Colombian border
stories.body: Nicolás Maduro announced on January 31 the deployment of Operación Relámpago del Catatumbo in northern Táchira and the Catatumbo river area of Zulia state along the Colombian border, as part of the Escudo Bolivariano 2025 plan. Maduro said the operation would carry out a complete clean-up of clandestine airstrips, coca crops and cocaine laboratories.

stories.headline: Brazilian Federal Police target customs-yard guards who recovered hidden drugs
stories.body: The Polícia Federal and Receita Federal executed search and seizure warrants on January 28 in Ponta Porã, Mato Grosso do Sul and in Rio Verde against outsourced customs security guards accused of dismantling an impounded vehicle at the customs yard in November 2024 to recover drugs concealed in its metal structure. One person was arrested in flagrante for illegal firearm possession.

stories.headline: Death of key witness exposes Paraguay-Colombia cocaine ties in prosecutor's murder
stories.body: InSight Crime examined the killing of Francisco Luis Correa Galeano, the main witness in the 2022 assassination of Paraguayan anti-mafia prosecutor Marcelo Pecci, found dead on January 3 in Bogotá's La Picota prison. Correa, tied to the Colombian Paisas and the Oficina de Envigado, had coordinated logistics and weapons for the killing and had named figures in Paraguayan cocaine trafficking and laundering networks.

stories.headline: Dutch ports report 38.6 tonnes of cocaine intercepted across 2024
stories.body: Dutch police, customs, the public prosecution service and port authorities jointly published 2024 seizure figures on January 23 for Rotterdam, Vlissingen and Moerdijk. Rotterdam accounted for 25,900 kilograms of cocaine, down from 45,506 kilograms in 2023, while the Zeeland-West-Brabant ports rose slightly to 12,664 kilograms. The total wholesale value of drugs intercepted exceeded 917 million euros.

stories.headline: Dutch customs seize 428 kilograms of cocaine in Peruvian fruit shipment
stories.body: Customs officers found 428 kilograms of cocaine hidden in a fruit consignment from Peru during a routine inspection at the port of Vlissingen, announced January 27. The container was destined for a company in Germany. The drugs, with a wholesale value of 10.7 million euros, were destroyed and no arrests were announced.

stories.headline: Malaysian police break up syndicate lacing vape cartridges with narcotics
stories.body: Johor police arrested five people — three Singaporeans, a Thai woman and a Malaysian — after an armed robbery investigation led them to a syndicate mixing narcotics into e-cigarette cartridges, announced January 27. Seizures included 2,277 grams of heroin, 1,063 grams of cannabis, 591 grams of ketamine, 174 grams of ecstasy powder and 13,673 millilitres of liquid drugs worth about 524,000 ringgit.

stories.headline: French Senate clears the articles of a landmark anti-narcotrafficking bill
stories.body: On the evening of January 29 the French Senate finished its article-by-article examination of a cross-party bill against drug trafficking, which creates a national anti-narcotics prosecutor's office, a high-security prison regime for major traffickers and expanded investigative powers. The final vote on the whole text was scheduled for February 4, 2025.

stories.headline: Cape Town anti-gang unit seizes 80,000 mandrax tablets
stories.body: SAPS Anti-Gang Unit officers raided a house in Beacon Valley, Mitchells Plain on January 22 and recovered 80,000 mandrax tablets worth about 4 million rand, hidden in a false compartment of a car parked at the property. A 26-year-old man and a 33-year-old woman were arrested. No total weight was released.

stories.headline: Cannabis worth 160,000 euros seized in County Cork
stories.body: Gardaí seized cannabis herb worth more than 160,000 euros, over 30,000 euros in cash and drug-preparation equipment during a planned search of a house in Carrigaline, County Cork on January 26. A man in his 30s was arrested and detained under the Criminal Justice (Drug Trafficking) Act 1996.
